races.name: Dobsons Gaskets Ebf Novice Stakes (gbb Race)
Simon's 20 Year Heart Transplant Anniversary Maiden Stakes (gbb Race)

runners_data.name: Master Of Delphi
runners_data.note: A hold-up operator with the class edge on paper at OR 120, though his sole run on similar Good ground produced a fifth and his trainer's 14-day record of 0/8 is poor; 43 days off the track and only one career run means he is largely unknown quantity, but the raw ability is there if he has progressed.

runners_data.name: Stoneacre Joe
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's string is in decent form (8/73 in 14 days) and this horse has placed twice on Good ground over 6f in recent starts, showing course-distance suitability; a hold-up style that lends itself to a late-pace scenario, though his -22845 form string shows inconsistency and he has struggled on softer ground variants.

runners_data.name: Indefensible
runners_data.note: Her role as the race's only front-runner gives her a tactical gift, but the STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) highlights she is stepping into this lead role somewhat out of character — she has raced over 7-8f in her recent history, and her ability to truly boss a 6f trip from the front is unproven; Ollie Pears sends her out just 10 days after her last run, which at least signals she is fit and ready.

runners_data.name: Valor Spirit
runners_data.note: Bryan Smart's runner has a consistent placed record at 6f including a recent second on Good ground, and Paul Mulrennan is an experienced handler of pace races at northern tracks; she maps prominently and will likely settle just behind Indefensible, giving her a prime position to pounce if the leader weakens, though her 8/10 sim-going placed record shows she finishes rather than wins.

runners_data.name: Black Orchid
runners_data.note: Richard & Peter Fahey's lightly-raced filly carries the intrigue of two consecutive seconds on Good ground over 6f — she clearly handles these conditions well under Oisin Orr, who rides her for the first time here; the unknown factor is whether she is capable of converting her placed form into a first career win, but the tactical profile suits a race where one horse leads alone.

races.paceDynamic: Indefensible is the sole confirmed front-runner in a field of five on Good ground at Ripon over 6f, meaning the pace is entirely in her hands — she can dictate an unchallenged, controlled tempo from the off. With both Valor Spirit and potentially Stoneacre Joe likely to push up to track her, the race should settle into a tight lead-prominent pocket through the first half, with Master Of Delphi and Black Orchid releasing from hold-up positions off the back. The critical caveat is Indefensible's history on this distance (3 of her last 5 runs over 8f), suggesting her ability to truly dominate over 6f is unproven and her front-running role here may be one of convenience rather than strength. This race shape — a single, unhurried pace-setter controlling an honest but uncontested gallop — ultimately favours horses with a late turn of foot coming from off the pace, particularly any hold-up runner capable of threading through in the final furlong as the leaders begin to roll back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Indefensible bowls along unchallenged and sets a steady, sustainable pace that she can maintain into the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Indefensible dictates from pillar to post on her own terms, with no rival willing to burn her off early, and the closing hold-up horses find the winner already gone when they make their move. Hold-up runners who lack the acceleration to reel in a horse that has rated its own effort perfectly are left chasing a ghost, and prominent trackers like Valor Spirit pick up the minor positions.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Swoop Late
scenarios.trigger: If Indefensible goes too steady and leaves a vacuum that allows the hold-up horses to build momentum before the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Master Of Delphi or Black Orchid, both running from off the pace, find clear daylight in the final two furlongs and pick off a tiring leader who has burned a little too freely mid-race. Black Orchid's consistent placed form on identical Good ground over 6f makes her particularly dangerous in this shape, and Master Of Delphi's class advantage on OR gives him the raw ability to swallow up a modest pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Late
scenarios.trigger: If Indefensible sets a fraction too hot early, given her limited stamina profile at 6f, and the leaders crumble inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Valor Spirit, who has been consistently placed at this distance on similar ground, is well-placed to capitalise tracking just off the pace as the front-runner fades, while Stoneacre Joe has the placed form at 6f on Good to pick up pieces. The principals come back to the hold-up horses, making this a rare scenario where everyone benefits from the tempo miscalculation at the front.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddled Messy Contest
scenarios.trigger: If Valor Spirit challenges Indefensible for the early lead and creates an uncharacteristically contested pace for such a small field.
scenarios.body: The race loses its shape entirely, the front two compromise each other's stamina, and an untidy contest opens up the race for whoever has been settled best in rear — likely Black Orchid tracking smoothly under Oisin Orr. Stoneacre Joe has the placed form to capitalise on chaos at this course if timing is right, though his inconsistent recent form is a concern.

watchPoints.text: Watch Indefensible's opening splits — if she is allowed to bowl along entirely unchallenged through the first two furlongs, she could be very hard to reel in and the race could be won and lost before the straight.

Black Orchid's two career runs have both been placed on identical Going and distance; if Oisin Orr can get her switched off in rear and deliver a clean run in the final furlong, she is the most likely horse to ambush the leader late.

Valor Spirit's prominent position could turn into a trap — if she tracks Indefensible too close and over-races, she risks emptying before the line; watch whether Mulrennan settles her a length or two off the front or allows her to press on.

Stoneacre Joe has gone 0/6 on Going described as Good in his recent history despite two placed efforts — his best form has come when conditions have eased slightly, so his true chance here on Good ground may be marginally overstated by his recent placed form at the trip.

Master Of Delphi's trainer angle is weak (0/8 in 14 days for Quinn) and he is 43 days off the track with only one prior run — if he shows any greenness or needs the run, his class advantage on paper could be neutralised entirely in a race this small.

races.name: Ripon Bell-ringer Handicap Stakes (gbbplus Race)

runners_data.name: Spioradalta
runners_data.note: The one confirmed front runner in this field; Mark Walford's six-year-old has winning form at 10f on Good and is stepping up to 1m4f, which may stretch her stamina — her ability to control tempo is her greatest asset but the extra distance is an unknown quantity at this level under 138lbs.
runners_data.comment: A two-time winner in its last six starts, most recently three starts back, and has run over today's trip and going before. Only 6th last time out, but a rating of 92 (fourth of eight) still puts him right in this after a 21-day break.

runners_data.name: Star Harbour
runners_data.note: Oisin Orr partners this eight-year-old for Adrian McGuinness who has returned 3/29 in the past 14 days; the visor is a notable piece of headgear and the horse has solid placed form at 1m4f on Good and Soft, though the low strike rate from similar ground form (0W1P) tempers expectations.
runners_data.comment: A second two starts back stands out in its last six starts, and this gelding has already run over today's trip and going before. Yet to win in that sequence, he tops our figures at 98 and wears a visor again following a 20-day break.

runners_data.name: Haku
runners_data.note: Silvestre De Sousa takes the ride on this Mark Loughnane-trained seven-year-old who has been off for 171 days — the significant layoff is the primary concern, though he has winning form at 1m4f on Tapeta and arrives fit enough to race prominently; how he handles the return after nearly six months off is the key question.
runners_data.comment: Third two starts back, and a winner three starts back, but only 7th last time out following a 171-day absence. Has run over today's trip and going before, and rated 97 (second of eight) he remains a leading threat fitness permitting.

runners_data.name: Elsass
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's four-year-old has won back-to-back at 11f and is clearly in form (T14: 7/66), but his true racing style is that of a hold-up horse — he has been repositioned into midfield on the map because this field cannot accommodate all its rear-of-field types at the back, which means he may race in an unnatural position that tempers how freely he can express his best form.
runners_data.comment: Won two starts back, and again three starts back, but was unplaced last time out. Has run over today's trip and going before, though a rating of 87 (seventh of eight) makes him hard to fancy after 14 days off.

runners_data.name: Prince Of The Seas
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's four-year-old ran only seven days ago and carries the tongue-tie; his best recent form is at 1m3f-1m4f on Good ground (2W5P from 14 runs in similar conditions) and Mark Winn is capable, making this genuinely suited horse one to respect if stamina becomes the deciding factor.
runners_data.comment: Second last time out, and third two starts back, though yet to win in six starts and wears a tongue-tie again. Ran over today's trip and going before just seven days ago, and rated 93 (third of eight) he's a leading threat.

runners_data.name: Salamanca City
runners_data.note: James Fanshawe has a strong 14-day record (4/15) and Daniel Muscutt is a quality booking; Salamanca City has won twice at 1m2f on Good ground and the step to 1m4f is a question, but his prominent racing style and recent course-and-distance placed form make him naturally well positioned to exploit a steady gallop.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out and has two runner-up efforts among her last five starts. Also ran over today's trip and going before, though a rating of 88 (sixth of eight) makes this more of a midfield claim after 43 days off.

runners_data.name: Per Contra
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's five-year-old holds the hood (p headgear) and raced seven days ago, but his recent record shows a string of poor runs including a 20th at 1m2f on Good; he is a genuine hold-up horse by profile, mapped into midfield due to the volume of rear-of-field types in this race, and that forced positional change works against him given his inconsistent recent form.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in six starts, though a third four starts back is the highlight of a mixed sequence. Has run over today's trip and going before, returns quickly after seven days, and a rating of 90 (fifth of eight) gives him a fair chance without standing out.

runners_data.name: Yafreh
runners_data.note: The sole three-year-old in the field, trained by Richard & Peter Fahey (T14: 4/43) and ridden by Cam Hardie; with an unknown running style and all four career runs at 1m2f-1m4f returning placed form, the light weight of 115lbs is an advantage but the step into open handicap company against older horses requires a significant step forward in form.
runners_data.comment: Twice second in his last four starts, including last time out, but yet to win and rated bottom of the field on 75 (eighth of eight). Has run over today's distance before, though that form makes him hard to fancy following a 17-day break.

races.paceDynamic: Spioradalta is the lone confirmed front runner in this eight-runner 1m4f handicap and, with no genuine pace rival prepared to dispute the lead, she can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good ground that rarely gets truly honest. Haku and Salamanca City will press forward into prominent positions, but they are more likely to track than to fight Spioradalta for the lead, meaning the fractions are set by one horse and are likely to be steady rather than searching. That scenario — a single horse controlling tempo from the front with a compressed midfield group behind — classically favours the hold-up horse who can produce a single, powerful late run when the pace is wound up in the straight, or alternatively the prominent racer with stamina to kick at the right moment. Note that Elsass and Per Contra are genuine hold-up types who have been mapped into midfield because this field carries more hold-up horses than can physically sit at the rear; both are more likely to be racing closer to the pace than their natural style demands, which dilutes the potency of any late-surge scenario. The tactical verdict is clear: a steady pace controlled by Spioradalta favours horses with stamina and a sustained galloping style who can sit prominently or mid-division and pick off the leader in the closing stages — prominent racers with a proven staying profile are best placed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Spioradalta Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Spioradalta leads at a steady tempo and the prominent group settles without pressuring her early.
scenarios.body: Spioradalta dictates every yard on her own terms, the gallop stays modest into the straight, and the race becomes a test of tactical speed and jumping ability over the last two furlongs rather than raw stamina; horses with a prominent position and a reliable finishing kick are best served. Salamanca City and Haku, both with form near the pace at this sort of distance, are well placed to pounce if the leader's stamina or concentration wavers late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Stamina Test Develops Gradually
scenarios.trigger: If Haku or Salamanca City applies enough early pressure that the pace becomes genuinely honest from halfway.
scenarios.body: A more searching gallop removes the pure speed element from the finish and turns proceedings into a test of who gets home strongest over the final three furlongs on Good ground at 1m4f; this plays directly into the hands of horses with proven staying form and a history of finishing races out. Prince Of The Seas, whose best recent form is around 1m4f-1m5f in Good conditions, and Star Harbour, with good placed form at 1m4f, become more credible threats as fatigue separates the field.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Delivers Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final quarter-mile and creates a gap for a horse coming from well off the tempo.
scenarios.body: Despite Elsass and Per Contra being pushed closer to the pace than they would naturally prefer, a slow-early scenario still leaves some room for a late finishing run if the leaders stop sharply; Elsass, with back-to-back wins at this sort of grade and trip, retains the most raw ability to capitalise. However, both hold-up types are carrying the penalty of racing in an unfamiliar position throughout, which significantly undermines the reliability of this scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse — Front Enders Swamped
scenarios.trigger: If Spioradalta sets a genuinely quick early pace and ties up her rivals before the straight.
scenarios.body: In the unlikely event that the early fractions are fast enough to exhaust the prominent group, the freshest horses at the business end of the field will pick off fading rivals late; Yafreh, the lightly raced three-year-old with a modest weight and placed form at 1m4f on Good, could emerge as a surprise beneficiary despite unproven stamina at this level. Per Contra's course form is limited and his recent runs have been inconsistent, but he would also feature in this unlikely shape if energy reserves prove decisive.

watchPoints.text: Spioradalta's stamina at 1m4f is unproven — if she weakens rapidly from two furlongs out having controlled the pace, the entire race shape inverts and prominent-to-midfield horses could sweep past her in a heap.

Haku's 171-day absence is the longest layoff in the field by a considerable margin — watch for any signs of race rustiness in the first half of the race, as a prominent horse who fades could compromise the run of those directly behind him.

Elsass and Per Contra are both natural hold-up horses who may find themselves uncomfortably close to the pace given the lack of a large rear group; if either horse fights for a position or is checked in traffic mid-race, their late finishing run will be compromised.

Prince Of The Seas ran only seven days ago — monitor his paddock behaviour and early movement for any sign of residual fatigue, as a seven-day turnaround at 1m4f on Good ground could test his reserves if the pace becomes genuinely searching.

Yafreh's unknown running style (tagged U) means his early positioning is entirely unpredictable — he could end up anywhere from the front rank to the rear, and his exact placement in the first quarter-mile will determine whether he is a factor at all in the closing stages.

races.name: Sky Bet Go-racing-in-yorkshire Summer Festival Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Midnight Strike
runners_data.note: A 15-day turnaround for Jennie Candlish after a recent win on good ground encourages, and the tongue-pin helps; a deep hold-up type whose 10f good-ground form is solid, though against an uncontested front-runner the distance back may be decisive.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out after four below-the-frame efforts, and a rating of 84 (second of six) reflects that improvement. Has run over today's trip and going before from stall two, wears tongue-tie and cheekpieces again, and the leap forward makes this the pick after 15 days off.

runners_data.name: Qitaal
runners_data.note: Connor Beasley partners a horse with four places from eight 10f starts on good and excellent course-form consistency; a genuine hold-up operator who arrives 13 days fresh and needs a stronger pace than Wild Violet alone is likely to generate.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out, and again two starts back, with two runner-up efforts also among the last six starts. Ran over today's trip and going before from stall six, and a rating of 84 (third of six) makes him a leading threat after 13 days off.

runners_data.name: Yermanthere
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's veteran arrives 19 days between runs with a win at 10f on good ground in recent history; his true racing style is rear of field, but with the hold-up positions oversubscribed he is likely to find himself closer to midfield in traffic — a tactical compromise that marginally aids his cause if the race quickens sharply.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up last time out, having won two starts back, form that keeps him well involved. Ran over today's trip and going before from stall three, and a rating of 76 (fourth of six) makes him a leading threat after 19 days off.

runners_data.name: Wild Violet
runners_data.note: Michael Bell's three-year-old has won on good ground over 10f and run well at Ripon's trip before; she is the confirmed pace-setter and the style-fit tag reflects that her most natural role is prominent rather than outright leader — though with only five rivals and no challenger, she can dictate exactly as suits her.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out, and was runner-up two starts back, but she's now rated bottom of the field on 71 (sixth of six). Has run over today's trip and going before from stall four, though a 34-day absence adds to the concerns against this stronger-rated field.

runners_data.name: Lucky Hero
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's three-year-old steps back up to a mile and two after winning at seven furlongs on good ground; he is a natural hold-up horse competing in a field where that territory is crowded, meaning he is pushed forward on the map despite being most at home sitting last and finishing — his route to the winner's enclosure depends on pace materialising that simply may not arrive.
runners_data.comment: Won three starts back and was fourth last time out, and tops our figures on 84 (first of six). Has run over today's going before from stall one, though a 36-day absence is the obvious question mark.

runners_data.name: Poet's Dawn
runners_data.note: An 11-year-old for Tim Easterby, 12 days since a recent run and equipped with a visor, whose two wins from his last five on good ground show he retains ability; the prominent style suits this race shape and tracking Wild Violet closely from the outset gives him the best accessible path to the line.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out, and a winner four and six starts back, though rated only 74 (fifth of six). Has run over today's trip and going before from stall five, wears cheekpieces again, but is hard to fancy after 12 days off.

races.paceDynamic: Wild Violet is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with only Poet's Dawn likely to press from a prominent position, she faces no meaningful early challenge and can dictate a comfortable, sustainable gallop over this 1m2f flat circuit at Ripon. With the pace controlled and uncontested, the race will be run at an even tempo rather than a searching test, which typically compresses the finish and rewards those positioned closest to the action rather than those coming from the deepest ground. Midnight Strike, Qitaal, Yermanthere, and Lucky Hero are all genuine hold-up types but the field contains more hold-up horses than can all sit in their natural rear positions; Lucky Hero and Yermanthere have been redistributed to midfield on the map, though in practice both are likely to be held up and covering ground late — neither is guaranteed to find room swiftly enough against a tempo set by Wild Violet. This race shape — a lone front-runner dictating an honest but unexaggerated gallop — most directly favours prominent types who can track the leader without burning energy, with genuine closers needing an unusually strong finish to reel them in.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Wild Violet Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Wild Violet is allowed to stride clear from the front and set a fair but manageable pace with only Poet's Dawn in attendance.
scenarios.body: Wild Violet controls every yard, the tempo remains measured, and those tracking closely into the straight hold the decisive positional advantage heading into the final two furlongs. Prominent horses who can sustain their effort around the turn — particularly Poet's Dawn if fit at age 11 — are best placed, while deep closers face too much to make up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Swamp The Line
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is deceptively strong enough that Wild Violet's advantage is neutralised turning for home, inviting the closers to rattle home.
scenarios.body: Qitaal's consistent 10-furlong form and Midnight Strike's finishing burst give both the profile to swoop late if there is a genuine end-to-end gallop to aim at. The flat Ripon straight gives finishers a clear sightline but a single uncontested front-runner rarely generates enough pace for this shape to dominate.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Movers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Lucky Hero or Yermanthere manage to secure a handy position and produce a well-timed late run after being reshuffled through the field.
scenarios.body: Both horses are true hold-up types operating out of their natural position, so this scenario requires the pace to suit and the draw to allow them clean daylight — a conditional combination. Lucky Hero's win over 7f on good gives him tactical speed if ridden aggressively, but stepping up in trip and acting against his natural style tempers confidence.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Two Fade, Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If Wild Violet and Poet's Dawn are caught wide or asked for an excessive early effort and both capitulate inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: This is the least likely shape given Wild Violet's ability to control proceedings with a small field and open track, but if she overcooks the early fractions on good ground, the finishers inherit the prize. Even then, closers redistributed to midfield must produce clean passages to benefit fully.

watchPoints.text: Wild Violet's early fractions are critical — if Oisin Orr elects to go very fast from the front with no pressure, she could steal an unassailable lead that none of the hold-up horses can close down.

Lucky Hero and Yermanthere are both natural hold-up horses in a race where the rear positions are overcrowded; watch for a bunching incident in the early stages as they compete for the same ground at the back.

Poet's Dawn at age 11 must match Wild Violet's pace from flag-fall — if the pace proves too hot for him to sustain contact, the entire prominent profile of the race collapses and the scenario calculus shifts.
Qitaal's four-place record over 10f on good is consistent but winless; Connor Beasley will need a well-judged pace from Wild Violet to set up the finishing test that unlocks this horse's best effort.

races.name: Sky Bet For The Fans Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Cadarn
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner in tongue-tie who posted a win over this C&D trip on Good recently; Kevin Ryan's yard is 1/25 in the last 14 days suggesting a quieter spell, but on today's terms Cadarn gets a soft lead and his C&D win (1/8f/GOO in last five) is the most relevant piece of form on the card.
runners_data.comment: Cadarn won last time out and heads this field on a rating of 87. He has raced over today's trip and going before, and the sole concern is a yard currently managing just a 1/25 strike rate over the last fortnight.

runners_data.name: Jimmy Speaking
runners_data.note: Chris Dwyer's yard is 1/4 in the last 14 days and De Sousa takes the ride, a meaningful booking upgrade; won at 7f on Standard and placed twice at 8f on Good, so the trip and surface suit, and racing prominently he can track the tempo without over-committing early.
runners_data.comment: Jimmy Speaking flopped to ninth last time out but that followed two wins in the three starts before, form that underpins a rating of 86. He has raced over today's trip and going before, with a 43-day break the main danger to his readiness.

runners_data.name: Farasi Lane
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old who has run all five recent starts at Southwell on Standard, so the switch to Good turf at Ripon is a significant question mark; natural hold-up style in a race where hold-up horses face congestion at the rear, and Hammond's yard is 0/4 in the last 14 days — context points away from him today.
runners_data.comment: Farasi Lane has been metronomic this campaign, fifth last time out and fifth again two starts back, with a win six starts back. He has raced over today's trip and going before, and a strong speed rating of 84 makes him a leading danger on a rating of 83.

runners_data.name: Sir Paul Ramsey
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's operation has strong overall numbers (7/66 in 14 days) and Jack Callan claims 3lb, keeping the weight manageable; races from the back and handles Good ground (2W in similar going from 15 runs), but his recent form string shows 7-6-11 and he needs a pace shape to materialise that may not arrive.
runners_data.comment: Sir Paul Ramsey was seventh last time out and sixth two starts back, modest form that leaves him without a win in his last six starts. He has raced over today's trip and going before, and a rating of 80 keeps him competitive in this line-up without standing out.

runners_data.name: Ben Lawers
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse whose last five runs are all over 10f, so dropping back to a flat mile is both a trip question and a role change; Simon Waugh's stable has no runners in the 14-day trainer data and the horse is mapped to midfield only because the rear is congested — discount this shown position as his natural operating zone.
runners_data.comment: Ben Lawers was unplaced last time out following a mixed run of sixths, though he does have a win six starts back. He has raced over today's trip and going before, and a rating of 81 keeps him among the leading dangers despite that recent blip.

runners_data.name: Garden Oasis
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's consistent handler (8/73 in 14 days) and David Allan, who knows the horse well, takes the ride; an 11-year-old who is remarkably consistent on Good ground (11 runs in similar going, 2W 5P), yet his true running style is hold-up and he has been mapped forward purely because the rear of this field is full — that displacement could cost him the late run he needs.
runners_data.comment: Garden Oasis was fourth last time out and fifth two starts back, respectable without getting close enough for a win in his last six starts. He has raced over today's trip and going before, and while a rating of 79 is workmanlike, he sits toward the back of this field.

runners_data.name: Jesmond Dawn
runners_data.note: Won over 8f on Good last time out (1/8f/GOO) and has three other placed efforts at the trip on Good or Yielding, so the surface and distance suit well; Grant Tuer is 4/11 in the last 14 days giving the yard a live presence, and racing prominently suits this mile trip on a flat track where hold-up horses can struggle for cover.
runners_data.comment: Jesmond Dawn won last time out, backed up by a runner-up effort four starts back, form that reads well on paper. Even so, he's the outsider here on a rating of 67, some way behind this field on our figures despite that recent win.

races.paceDynamic: Cadarn is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with only Jimmy Speaking and Jesmond Dawn as prominent types behind, faces minimal pressure to his lead — he can dictate a controlled, honest gallop on Good ground at Ripon over a flat mile. Jimmy Speaking and Jesmond Dawn will contest the early positions behind Cadarn, but the real crowding happens further back: Ben Lawers and Garden Oasis are genuine hold-up horses who are likely to be displaced forward simply because the rear of this field is congested, meaning their natural late runs may be compromised. The race shape is therefore moderate-tempo, single-file, with a sustained gallop rather than a dawdle or a sprint — Ripon's flat mile rewards horses who travel comfortably and pick up in the straight without needing a wall of pace to aim at. This shape strongly favours prominent-racing types who can track Cadarn at a manageable pace and quicken from a handy position in the home straight, rather than horses who need genuine strong fractions to deliver their finish.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Cadarn Leads, Prompt Chasers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Cadarn sets a controlled honest gallop and the prominent chasers travel smoothly to pounce approaching the furlong pole.
scenarios.body: Cadarn dictates from the front at a sustainable tempo, keeping fractions even enough to suit horses racing just behind him; Jimmy Speaking and Jesmond Dawn, both proven at this trip on Good, are ideally placed to pick off the leader inside the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Cadarn's gallop is slow enough to conserve energy and rivals leave their challenge too late.
scenarios.body: With minimal pressure on the leader throughout, Cadarn conserves enough fuel to repel all challengers in the short Ripon straight; his Good-ground form and the lack of any horse willing to force the pace early works directly in his favour.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Types Get Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or bunches, allowing Sir Paul Ramsey or redistributed runners to weave through late.
scenarios.body: A moderate or stop-start gallop creates a compressed field turning in, giving Sir Paul Ramsey and Garden Oasis — who handles Good ground well with five Good-ground runs in his last five — a narrow window to finish through gaps.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: True Hold-Up Horses Deliver
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong and the race fractures late, allowing Farasi Lane or Ben Lawers to finish past beaten rivals.
scenarios.body: This outcome requires a tempo significantly above what one uncontested front-runner typically generates, making it the least likely shape; Farasi Lane has been running at Southwell on Standard all season and faces a surface shift, while Ben Lawers is tagged as racing out of role and his recent form over 10f handicaps is poor.

watchPoints.text: Cadarn's sectionals early: if Shane Gray elects to dawdle and no one challenges, he could control the race from flag to finish and potentially steal the race — any runner drawn wide who cannot get up to challenge early is in trouble.

Jimmy Speaking's 43-day break is the key fitness concern: De Sousa's booking suggests he is fit enough to run a big race fresh, but monitor in the paddock for any sign of a ring-rusty run that leaves him short of a winning effort.

Garden Oasis and Ben Lawers are both natural hold-up horses forced to race in mid-division — if the pace is modest they will be neither prominent enough to pounce early nor far enough back to get a true late run, leaving them racing in no-man's land throughout.

Farasi Lane's going switch from Standard at Southwell to Good turf at Ripon is the most significant profile change in the race — watch his market movement to gauge confidence from the Hammond yard that he handles the surface.

Sir Paul Ramsey holds a 3lb claim via Jack Callan but has not won in six starts — if the pace is compressed turning in he is the most likely beneficiary of a bunched finish, but his recent form suggests he cannot be trusted to convert even if the shape goes his way.

races.name: Napoleons Casino And Restaurant Leeds Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Sparkling Pink
runners_data.note: Adrian Nicholls' filly has competitive similar-going form (placed once in three Good-ground runs) and gets back on a mile having shaped as though this trip suits; a genuine hold-up type who will need a strong enough pace to make her late run count — the quiet gallop set by Mohmentous is her chief concern.
runners_data.comment: Fourth last time out, and third three starts back, without a win in her last five starts. Has run over today's trip and going before from stall two, and a rating of 65 (second of nine) makes her a leading threat after 28 days off.

runners_data.name: Balmoral Boy
runners_data.note: Nigel Tinkler three-year-old returning after 33 days with only two similar-going runs behind him and no wins or places in five starts; hold-up style suits a race where the pace is genuine but his form figures (3-6-5-8-11) suggest he is struggling to hit the frame at present.
runners_data.comment: Third five starts back is the standout in an otherwise modest sequence without a win in his last five starts. Has run over today's distance before from stall five, but a rating of 57 (eighth of nine) makes him hard to fancy after 33 days off.

runners_data.name: Mohmentous
runners_data.note: The race's only confirmed pace-setter and the central tactical figure, operating slightly outside his natural prominent comfort zone at this longer trip; his trainer Ollie Sangster is firing well (4/19 in 14 days) and the uncontested lead on good ground over a mile at Ripon is a powerful positional advantage — STYLE_FIT flag is noted but the race is set up perfectly for him.
runners_data.comment: Won three starts back, and again four starts back, with a third last time out too. Has run over today's trip and going before from stall eight, and a rating of 64 (third of nine) makes him a leading threat after 16 days off.

runners_data.name: Aurelune
runners_data.note: Richard & Fahey yard in solid 14-day form (4/43); in truth a pure hold-up runner who has been pushed into a midfield map slot because the rear of this field is crowded — only one place from five similar-ground starts means the form is thin, and the shortened finish time on good ground may catch her out.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out, and again four starts back, either side of modest efforts, without a win in her last five starts. Has run over today's distance before from stall seven, but a rating of 59 (seventh of nine) makes her hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Delevingne Dream
runners_data.note: Harry Eustace three-year-old with a fades-in-finish flag and a bleak form string of 0-07; the good ground is fine but she has twice finished last at this course/distance equivalent, and 30 days off has not yet translated into improvement — hard to recommend.
runners_data.comment: Unplaced in two of her last three starts, with a seventh the best of those efforts, and now bottom of our figures on 47 (ninth of nine). Has run over today's distance before from stall three, but this looks a stiff task following a 30-day absence.

runners_data.name: Singarda
runners_data.note: Tony Coyle & Kaine Wood runner wearing a tongue-tie; placed into midfield by the pace map but is a genuine rear-of-field operator, and five Good-ground starts without a win or place underlines the difficulty of her task in a race where the pace is unlikely to be strong enough to play to her strengths.
runners_data.comment: A modest sequence without a win in his last five starts, though a rating of 64 (fourth of nine) keeps him firmly involved. Has run over today's trip and going before from stall one, wears tongue-tie and cheekpieces again, after 15 days off.

runners_data.name: Vega's Virtue
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's filly has a genuinely compelling profile — a course-and-distance winner (1/8f/GOO in recent hist) wearing a hood, and David Allan takes the ride; she sits closer to the pace than her hold-up label suggests in practice, and her seven Good-ground runs include three places, making her the most dangerous of the held-up types.
runners_data.comment: Won three starts back and finished third two starts back, though only eighth last time out. Has run over today's trip and going before from stall six, and a rating of 62 (fifth of nine) leaves her a fair midfield claim after 15 days off.

runners_data.name: Sovereign Bright
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston yard busy (7/66 in 14 days) and the handicapper has her at OR 56 after a placed run at Stamina trips; her natural hold-up style is honest — headgear listed as 'h' — and she has finished in the frame at 10f, so the drop to a mile may sharpen her finish, though good ground form is limited (4 runs, 0W1P).
runners_data.comment: Tops our figures on 66 (first of nine), and has already run over today's trip and going before. Modest last time out and two starts back, but a smart pair of thirds further back mark her out as the one to beat from stall nine, hood retained.

runners_data.name: Trucial Pearl
runners_data.note: Michael & David Easterby three-year-old running just two days after her last start (visor worn), which is worth noting as a fitness flag; a winner over 8f on good ground and shows prominent/handy tendencies that could see her slot in just behind Mohmentous — the visor and quick turnaround are the key talking points here.
runners_data.comment: Fourth last time out just two days ago, having won two starts back, so continues on a quick turnaround. Has run over today's trip and going before from stall four, wears a visor again, and a rating of 61 (sixth of nine) leaves her a fair midfield claim.

races.paceDynamic: Mohmentous is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner mile handicap and, critically, faces no genuine challenger for the lead — Trucial Pearl has shown some prominence but is unlikely to push hard enough to pressurise, meaning Mohmentous can dictate a measured, controlled gallop from the front on good ground at Ripon. With the pace sedate and sustainable, the race is likely to develop in a strung-out fashion around Ripon's sweeping turns, with the tempo not rising meaningfully until the home straight, gifting the leader a significant advantage in terms of energy conservation. The field contains a cluster of genuine hold-up types — Aurelune, Singarda, Vega's Virtue, Sovereign Bright and Sparkling Pink — who are all mapped closer than their natural position because the rear of the race is over-populated; those most likely to actually secure a handy pitch are Vega's Virtue (headgear, prominent course form) and Trucial Pearl (freshness, 2-day turnaround, natural early foot). The race shape strongly favours the patient hold-up horse with a sharp turn of foot who can launch from midfield into the straight, but the lone pace-setter who controls tempo from the front — Mohmentous — is the primary tactical beneficiary given the absence of early pressure.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Mohmentous Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Mohmentous secures a soft lead and is never seriously pressured through the first six furlongs.
scenarios.body: Mohmentous sets a comfortable gallop that saps the energy of hold-up horses forced to close from a long way back, and the good ground suits his ability to quicken away when asked in the straight after a race run on his terms.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just fast enough to find out Mohmentous, and a genuinely patient closer produces a sustained run through the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Sparkling Pink or Vega's Virtue — the two hold-up types with the most convincing similar-going form — launch from off the pace having been better placed than most of the other closers, delivering a late challenge that the front-runner cannot repel.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Trucial Pearl pushes up to sit just behind Mohmentous early and the two pull clear of the hold-up pack in the straight.
scenarios.body: The hold-up horses, compressed into a midfield cluster, fail to produce enough acceleration on a good surface where the pace has been too steady, leaving the two prominent types to fight it out in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Quickens Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses suddenly and a redistributed mid-division runner finds daylight late.
scenarios.body: Sovereign Bright or Singarda, both racing closer than natural but finding an unobstructed run in the straight, capitalise on a field that has bunched up — though their STYLE_FIT flags mean this is the lowest-probability shape.

watchPoints.text: Mohmentous leads unchallenged — if Jack Callan (3) is allowed to dictate without any horse committing to chase, the sedate gallop could make the leader almost impossible to catch in the straight.

Vega's Virtue's course-and-distance win on good ground combined with David Allan's experience makes her the most credible threat to the front-runner, and any sign of a stronger-than-expected pace would significantly boost her chance.

Trucial Pearl's two-day turnaround is unusual — watch for any market support or withdrawal; if she pushes up to press Mohmentous early the entire pace dynamic changes and closes up to three or four horses.

The midfield cluster of redistributed hold-up types (Aurelune, Singarda, Sovereign Bright, Sparkling Pink) will all need to thread through traffic in the straight — watch the draw and early positioning as Ripon's mile can favour those who find the rail.

Delevingne Dream carries a fades-in-finish flag and has shown nothing in three runs — watch for any drift in the market as a signal that connections are simply using this for experience rather than expecting a competitive effort.

races.name: Aldwark Manor Estate Luxury Yorkshire Hotel "confined" Handicap Stakes (For Horses Which Have Not Won A Race In 2026)

runners_data.name: Oasis Cover
runners_data.note: Ripon's straight 6f is the key: she has won over this trip on good ground and carries the sole confirmed lead role — Aiden Brookes will look to slide across and dictate, but the style-fit tag reminds that she maps here by default rather than being an out-and-out tearaway, so her finishing effort matters as much as the lead.
runners_data.comment: Oasis Cover was runner-up last time out but unplaced two starts back, a mixed recent sequence. She has raced over today's trip and going before, though a 28-day gap and a rating of 58 leave her needing more to break into the leading pack.

runners_data.name: Act Of Violence
runners_data.note: Silvestre De Sousa takes a hold-up horse into a race where rear positions are crowded; Tony Carroll's yard is in decent form (4/41 over 14 days) but the true running style sits further back than the map can place him, which materially reduces his chance of finding the run he needs.
runners_data.comment: Act Of Violence was fourth last time out, better than the eighth two starts back, though he remains without a win in his last five starts. He has raced over today's trip and going before, and a rating of 58 keeps him firmly in the pack.

runners_data.name: Jack Rabbit Slims
runners_data.note: Last run just four days ago — freshness is the question mark — but Tom Eaves partners a horse with a strong record of placing on good ground over 5-6f, and the tongue-tie/pad headgear suggests connections want him switched on early; genuinely holds up so needs a proper pace.
runners_data.comment: Jack Rabbit Slims was fourth last time out, having been second two starts back, still without a win in his last six starts. Back within just four days, he has raced over today's trip and going before, and a rating of 64 makes him one of the leading dangers.

runners_data.name: Mister Sky Blue
runners_data.note: Gemma Tutty's four-year-old finished second on good and good-to-soft over 6f and is one of the likelier horses to press Oasis Cover for the early prominent berth; Kaiya Fraser needs to get him into stride quickly to secure that position, and the course form over this trip is the chief asset.
runners_data.comment: Mister Sky Blue was ninth last time out, a big letdown after finishing second two starts back, and he remains without a win in his last five starts. He has raced over today's trip and going before, but a rating of 55 leaves him needing a bounce-back from midfield.

runners_data.name: Sergeant Mayer
runners_data.note: Nigel Tinkler's five-year-old hasn't run for 61 days — the layoff is the key concern — but the prominent style fits this race shape well, Alex Jary claims 3lb, and two wins and six places in his overall record on good ground suggest he handles conditions; needs to bounce straight back.
runners_data.comment: Sergeant Mayer was ninth last time out, sixth two starts back, without a win in his last five starts. He has raced over today's trip and going before and, despite a 61-day break, tops our figures on a rating of 65 as the leading threat.

runners_data.name: Get Up Everybody
runners_data.note: Paul Mulrennan on a Paul Midgley hold-up horse who has finished third or better in five of his last eight starts on good ground; the 15-day turnaround is fine, and if the pace is genuine he is one of the better-credentialled closers in the field to take advantage.
runners_data.comment: Get Up Everybody was fifth last time out, seventh two starts back, still without a win in his last five starts. He has raced over today's trip and going before, quickly back within fifteen days, and a rating of 64 keeps him among the leading dangers.

runners_data.name: Von Trotter
runners_data.note: Michael and David Easterby's three-year-old produced his only placed effort at 2/5f on standard and is stepping back from a 5-6f range; Billy Garritty rides, but four runs on good turf have not yielded a placed effort and the consistent finishing position of 6th-10th is a concern in a competitive handicap.
runners_data.comment: Von Trotter was sixth last time out and seventh two starts back, modest form on paper, though he has raced over today's trip and going before and carries a strong speed rating of 75. Fit after a 21-day break, a rating of 65 gives him solid claims.

runners_data.name: Hurstwood
runners_data.note: A nine-year-old who has finished 4th-11th across his last five starts, all on good ground over 6f at Ripon's level — Peter Niven sends him here with course familiarity as the angle, but this true hold-up horse is squeezed even further forward on the map than natural, and the age and recent form combine to make improvement hard to find.
runners_data.comment: Hurstwood was unplaced last time out and sixth two starts back, a run of form that leaves him without a win in his last five starts. He has raced over today's trip and going before, but a rating of 51 puts him near the bottom of this field.

runners_data.name: Indy's Angel
runners_data.note: Philip Kirby's four-year-old has shown genuine placed form on good ground (2nd twice in five runs), and the recent headgear change (tongue-tie) may sharpen her; Connor Beasley rides, and though she is a natural hold-up performer pushed into a midfield slot by the crowded rear, the 7f and 6f placed efforts suggest she acts on the ground.
runners_data.comment: Indy's Angel was runner-up last time out and again two starts back, yet to win in her last six starts despite that promise. She has raced over today's trip and going before, fit only ten days on, though a rating of 51 leaves her bottom of our figures.

runners_data.name: Long Shot
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's three-year-old has placed four times in ten runs on good ground at 6-7f, and David Allan's booking is a positive; the horse finds himself mapped ahead of his natural position because the field is rear-heavy, and the style-fit discount applies, but a track record of placing means he cannot be entirely dismissed if the pace is strong.
runners_data.comment: Long Shot was fourth last time out and second two starts back, consistent form without a win in his last six starts. He has raced over today's trip and going before, back within twelve days, and a rating of 52 keeps him firmly mid-pack.

runners_data.name: Lady Bouquet
runners_data.note: Philip Kirby sends out his second runner — last run just two days ago is eyecatching — and Lady Bouquet has placed in three of her last six on good ground over 5-6f; Cam Hardie rides a natural hold-up type who is pushed to a midfield slot by the weight of similar horses in this field, and the very quick turnaround adds an extra variable.
runners_data.comment: Lady Bouquet was fourth last time out and third two starts back, consistent without a win in her last six starts. She has raced over today's trip and going before, quick to reappear just two days on, though a rating of 51 leaves her towards the back of this field.

races.paceDynamic: Oasis Cover is the one confirmed front-runner in this field and, with no genuine rival to pressure her from the gates, she is set to control proceedings from the front at a sustainable gallop over Ripon's straight 6f on good ground. The three prominent types — Sergeant Mayer, Mister Sky Blue, and Oasis Cover herself — will contest the early positions, but with Oasis Cover's style mapped at lead, she holds the clearest route to a soft lead. This creates a race where the pace is honest but not searching, favouring those who can track the leader and produce a sustained run from two furlongs out rather than those relying on a late sprint off a crawl. The race shape therefore suits prominent racers and close-tracking midfielders over true hold-up horses; five runners (Act Of Violence, Hurstwood, Indy's Angel, Long Shot, and Lady Bouquet) are genuine hold-up types redistributed forward on the map because this field contains far more rear-dwellers than the shape can accommodate naturally — of the prominent spots behind Oasis Cover, Sergeant Mayer and Mister Sky Blue are most likely to actually secure them.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Oasis Cover Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Oasis Cover breaks cleanly and no rival attacks her early lead, she dictates a comfortable gallop and her rivals cannot close.
scenarios.body: She sets her own fractions on the Good Ripon turf, building an advantage that proves beyond the hold-up horses caught in traffic; prominent types who track her closely are best placed to challenge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Apply Pressure
scenarios.trigger: If Sergeant Mayer or Mister Sky Blue push forward to challenge Oasis Cover through the early stages, the pace quickens and suits closers off a genuine gallop.
scenarios.body: A contested early duel lifts the tempo enough that hold-up horses can sustain meaningful runs in the final furlong; those with good sectionals on good ground benefit most.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Weaves Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves strong enough to string the field out and a gap opens in the straight, one of the redistributed hold-up horses finds room late.
scenarios.body: Lady Bouquet or Indy's Angel, both in decent form with multiple placed efforts on good ground, would be the likeliest beneficiaries if produced with a perfectly-timed run; the style-fit discount still applies given their forced positioning.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Midrace
scenarios.trigger: If Oasis Cover finds no pressure but also fails to sustain her gallop, the race bunches in the final two furlongs and becomes a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: A compressed finish over a flat straight suits the freshest legs regardless of style, making the lightly-raced or recently-rested runners momentarily dangerous; Von Trotter, stepping back in trip, could be involved.

watchPoints.text: Oasis Cover's early sectional — if she is not challenged through the first two furlongs and clears five lengths, the hold-up horses will have too much to do on this flat, straight track.
Sergeant Mayer's 61-day absence is the biggest unknown: if he is ring-rusty out of the gate, the prominent positions behind Oasis Cover fall to Mister Sky Blue alone, tightening the pace further.

With five horses tagged as redistributed hold-up types all needing late runs on a straight 6f, watch for crowding and interference in the final two furlongs as multiple horses make ground simultaneously.
Lady Bouquet's two-day turnaround is unusually sharp — monitor market moves closer to the off, as Kirby's intention with her may become clearer in the betting.
Jack Rabbit Slims' four-day turnaround and headgear (tongue-tie, pads) suggests connections want an immediate reaction; if he jumps well he could be closer to the pace than his hold-up tag implies.
